:::{#thm-markov}
#### Markov's inequality: a nonnegative random variable is at least a threshold with probability at most its expectation over the threshold

Let $X$ be a nonnegative [random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable)
with a finite [expectation](expectation.qmd#def-expectation) $\E{X}$, <!-- check-term-links: allow: finite means a real number here, not a finite set -->
and let $a$ be a positive number.
Then the [probability](probability-basics.qmd#def-probability) that $X$ is at least $a$
is at most $\E{X}$ divided by $a$
[@wikipedia_markovs_inequality]:

$$
\Prf{X \ge a} \le \frac{\E{X}}{a}
$$

:::

::: proof

Because $X \ge 0$, every outcome satisfies $X \ge a \cdot \indic{\set{X \ge a}}$:
when $X \ge a$ the right side is $a \le X$, and otherwise it is $0 \le X$.
The expectation of a nonnegative random variable is nonnegative,
so by [linearity of expectation](expectation.qmd#thm-linearity-expectation),
and because the expectation of an indicator is the probability of its event,

$$
\E{X} - a \cdot \Prf{X \ge a}
= \E{X - a \cdot \indic{\set{X \ge a}}}
\ge 0
$$

and dividing by $a > 0$ gives the claim.

:::
